ION commenced operation of the ENTP carbon capture module on September 19, 2023. MEA was used as the carbon capture solvent to baseline the system before testing with ION’s proprietary solvents, ICE- 21™ and ICE-31®. The MEA campaign consisted of various parametric baseline tests, and the plant was operated for 12 hours a day on weekdays. The ICE-21™ campaign was run from October 2023 to February 2024. The ICE-21™ campaign commenced with a series of parametric tests designed to determine Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) related to ICE-21™. These tests included flue gas turndown, flue gas temperature turndown, and optimization of the liquid to gas ratio (L/G) to minimize the specific reboiler duty (SRD). Parametric testing was followed by a long-term steady-state test intended to assess the degradation and performance of ICE-21™ over prolonged periods. ION switched to 24/7 operations for the long-term testing to better simulate real-world conditions. The ICE-31® campaign began in February 2024 and ran until February 2025. Parametric testing was run from February to July 2024. Tests included the same ones performed for ICE-21™ with the addition of high-pressure stripper operations. Evaluation of the performance of ICE-31® at these different conditions is critical for understanding and predicting behavior at a commercial scale where flue gas conditions can vary significantly depending on the required load on the power plant during non-standard demand hours. Long-term steady-state testing also included activated carbon adsorption filtration for ICE-31®. Long-term solvent performance is another critical learning in ION Clean Energy 1 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT preparation for commercial-scale deployment where carbon capture systems are expected to operate for years, and any solvent addition or reclamation can have significant impacts on project costs. ION Clean Energy 2 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 2 Project Organization and Structure ION assembled a specialized and experienced team to complete this project. The project team was composed of ION, KMPS, who designed and constructed the modular pilot system, S&L, who provided the balance of plant design, and Calpine, who provided the LMEC as the NGCC host site. The ION team was led by Andrew Awtry, Ph.D., Senior Vice President of Engineering, during the first and second Budget Periods as the principal investigator (PI) on this project. Dr. Awtry has experience with a prior company (Neumann Systems Group) as the Principal Investigator on the successful design, construction, and testing of an engineering-scale carbon capture demonstration at a power station (DE-FE0007528). For ION, he has acted as technical lead for the large-scale pilot testing at the Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM) (DE-FE0013303) and two design and costing studies to implement a commercial carbon capture system at an existing power station (DE-FE0031595 & DE-FE0031840). His role was to ensure adequate communication between all partner organizations and manage the project according to the project schedule.
